title: Meeting someone new
context: You're at a friend's dinner party. A young man you haven't met walks over to you.
goal: Greet him, exchange names, ask how he is, and say goodbye.

line.urdu: سنیے!
line.en: Excuse me!

choices.feedback: Perfect — that is the polite way to answer "Suniye!".
Fine! "Ji, boliye" (yes, go ahead) sounds a little more welcoming.
That means goodbye — you've only just met! Answer with "Ji, boliye" instead.

line.roman: Mera naam Bilal hai. Aap ka naam kya hai?
line.urdu: میرا نام بلال ہے۔ آپ کا نام کیا ہے؟
line.en: My name is Bilal. What is your name?

choices.feedback: Great introduction. "Mera naam" is the same for every speaker.
He already told you his name (Bilal). Now he's asking yours.
He asked your name, not how you are. Listen for "naam".

line.roman: Aapse mil kar khushi hui! Aap kaise hain?
line.urdu: آپ سے مل کر خوشی ہوئی! آپ کیسے ہیں؟
line.en: Nice to meet you! How are you?

choices.roman: Main theek hoon, shukriya. Aap sunayein?
choices.urdu: میں ٹھیک ہوں، شکریہ۔ آپ سنائیں؟
choices.feedback: Excellent — you answered and bounced the question back.
Correct! Adding "Aap sunayein?" would keep the conversation going.
"Kaise hain?" means "how are you?" — "yes" doesn't answer it.

line.roman: Main bhi theek hoon, shukriya. Aap kahan se hain?
line.urdu: میں بھی ٹھیک ہوں، شکریہ۔ آپ کہاں سے ہیں؟
line.en: I'm fine too, thanks. Where are you from?

choices.feedback: Nice. Swap in your own city any time.

choices.roman: Mujhe samajh nahi aaya. Aahista boliye.
choices.urdu: مجھے سمجھ نہیں آیا۔ آہستہ بولیے۔
choices.en: I didn't understand. Please speak slowly.
choices.feedback: Totally fine — asking someone to slow down is a key skill.

line.roman: Ji, zaroor. Aap... kahan... se... hain?
line.urdu: جی، ضرور۔ آپ... کہاں... سے... ہیں؟
line.en: Of course. Where... are... you... from?

choices.feedback: Well done — you recovered and answered.

line.roman: Acha! Bohat acha. Chalo, phir milenge!
line.urdu: اچھا! بہت اچھا۔ چلو، پھر ملیں گے!
line.en: Oh nice! Very good. Okay, see you again!

choices.urdu: جی، پھر ملیں گے۔ خدا حافظ!
choices.feedback: A warm, natural goodbye.

choices.roman: Aapse mil kar khushi hui. Khuda hafiz!
choices.urdu: آپ سے مل کر خوشی ہوئی۔ خدا حافظ!
choices.feedback: Lovely — polite and friendly.

line.urdu: خدا حافظ!
line.en: Goodbye!

nodes.end: You greeted Bilal, introduced yourself, answered his questions and said goodbye.

title: Visiting your aunt
context: Your mother's sister (your Khala) has come to visit. She's warm, talkative and asks about the family.
goal: Greet an elder respectfully, answer family questions and accept or decline tea.

line.urdu: بیٹا، سب خیریت ہے؟
line.en: Dear, is everything well?

nodes.note: Elders often call younger people "beta" (lit. son) as a term of affection — for boys and girls.

choices.roman: Ji, Khala, sab khairiyat hai, shukriya.
choices.urdu: جی خالہ، سب خیریت ہے، شکریہ۔
choices.en: Yes, Auntie, all is well, thanks.
choices.feedback: Respectful and warm — exactly right with an elder.
Fine, though adding "Khala" and "shukriya" sounds warmer with an elder.
Far too casual for an aunt! Save "yaar" for friends.

line.urdu: امی ابو کیسے ہیں؟
line.en: How are your mum and dad?

choices.feedback: "Woh ... hain" — plural for two people (and respectful).
She asked about your parents (ammi abbu), not you. Try "Woh theek hain".

line.roman: Aap ke kitne behen bhai hain? Main bhool gayi!
line.urdu: آپ کے کتنے بہن بھائی ہیں؟ میں بھول گئی!
line.en: How many brothers and sisters do you have? I forgot!

nodes.note: "Bhool gayi" — Khala is a woman, so she says gayi.

choices.roman: Mere do bhai hain aur ek behen hai.
choices.urdu: میرے دو بھائی ہیں اور ایک بہن ہے۔
choices.en: I have two brothers and one sister.
choices.feedback: Great sentence — notice "hain" for two brothers and "hai" for one sister.
You probably know how many siblings you have! Try "Mere ... bhai hain".

line.urdu: واہ! چائے پئیں گے؟
line.en: Wonderful! Will you have some tea?

choices.feedback: Accepting tea graciously is always welcome.
Polite. Expect elders to insist a little — that's part of hospitality.

line.urdu: یہ لو، گرم گرم چائے۔
line.en: Here you go, nice hot tea.

choices.roman: Bohat shukriya, Khala. Bohat mazay ki hai!
choices.urdu: بہت شکریہ خالہ۔ بہت مزے کی ہے!
choices.en: Thank you so much, Auntie. It's delicious!
choices.feedback: "Mazay ki" agrees with chai (feminine). Lovely.

line.urdu: اچھا، ٹھیک ہے۔ پھر کبھی!
line.en: Alright then. Another time!

choices.feedback: Polite and warm.

line.roman: Khuda hafiz, beta. Ammi ko salaam kehna!
line.urdu: خدا حافظ بیٹا۔ امی کو سلام کہنا!
line.en: Goodbye, dear. Give my regards to your mum!

nodes.end: You greeted your aunt respectfully, talked about family and handled tea like a pro.

title: Please speak slowly
context: A friendly neighbour stops you in the street and starts talking quickly.
goal: Admit you didn't understand, ask him to slow down, then introduce yourself.

line.roman: Aap naye aaye hain is mohallay mein? Kab shift huay?
line.urdu: آپ نئے آئے ہیں اس محلے میں؟ کب شفٹ ہوئے؟
line.en: Are you new to this neighbourhood? When did you move in?

choices.roman: Maaf kijiye, mujhe samajh nahi aaya. Aahista boliye.
choices.urdu: معاف کیجیے، مجھے سمجھ نہیں آیا۔ آہستہ بولیے۔
choices.en: Sorry, I didn't understand. Please speak slowly.
choices.feedback: Perfect — polite, honest and useful.
Nodding along is tempting, but it usually leads to more questions you can't follow.
Walking away won't help! Ask him to slow down instead.

line.roman: Acha! To kab shift huay? Kis gali mein?
line.urdu: اچھا! تو کب شفٹ ہوئے؟ کس گلی میں؟
line.en: Oh good! So when did you move? Which street?

choices.roman: Maaf kijiye, mujhe samajh nahi aaya. Aahista boliye, please.
choices.urdu: معاف کیجیے، مجھے سمجھ نہیں آیا۔ آہستہ بولیے، پلیز۔
choices.en: Sorry, I didn't understand. Please speak slowly.
choices.feedback: Good recovery. It's never too late to ask.

line.urdu: جی، جی۔ آپ... نئے... ہیں؟
line.en: Yes, yes. Are... you... new?

choices.roman: Ji haan. Mujhe thori Urdu aati hai.
choices.urdu: جی ہاں۔ مجھے تھوڑی اردو آتی ہے۔
choices.en: Yes. I know a little Urdu.
choices.feedback: Great — telling people you're learning makes them slow down naturally.
Fine to ask again!

line.urdu: آپ۔ نئے۔ ہیں؟ نیو؟
line.en: You. New. Are? New?

choices.roman: Ji haan! Mujhe thori Urdu aati hai.
choices.urdu: جی ہاں! مجھے تھوڑی اردو آتی ہے۔
choices.en: Yes! I know a little Urdu.
choices.feedback: You got there.

line.roman: Koi baat nahi! Aap ki Urdu achi hai. Mera naam Rashid hai.
line.urdu: کوئی بات نہیں! آپ کی اردو اچھی ہے۔ میرا نام راشد ہے۔
line.en: No problem! Your Urdu is good. My name is Rashid.

choices.roman: Shukriya! Mera naam {name} hai. Aapse mil kar khushi hui.
choices.urdu: شکریہ! میرا نام {name} ہے۔ آپ سے مل کر خوشی ہوئی۔
choices.en: Thanks! My name is {name}. Nice to meet you.
choices.feedback: A great introduction.

line.roman: Mujhe bhi khushi hui. Koi kaam ho to batayein!
line.urdu: مجھے بھی خوشی ہوئی۔ کوئی کام ہو تو بتائیں!
line.en: Nice to meet you too. If you need anything, let me know!

nodes.end: You handled fast speech by asking politely for help — one of the most important skills for real conversations.

title: Ordering at a restaurant
context: You sit down at a busy local restaurant. A waiter comes over.
goal: Order food and a drink, comment on the meal and pay the bill.

line.urdu: جی، کیا لاؤں؟
line.en: What shall I bring you?

choices.roman: Mujhe chicken karahi aur do roti chahiye.
choices.urdu: مجھے چکن کڑاہی اور دو روٹی چاہیے۔
choices.en: I'd like chicken karahi and two rotis.
choices.feedback: Clear order using "Mujhe ... chahiye".
True, but the waiter still needs to know what you want!
You haven't ordered yet! Tell him what you'd like with "Mujhe ... chahiye".

line.roman: Ji, yeh menu dekhiye. Kya chahiye?
line.urdu: جی، یہ مینو دیکھیے۔ کیا چاہیے؟
line.en: Here, have a look at the menu. What would you like?

choices.roman: Mujhe chicken karahi aur do roti chahiye.
choices.urdu: مجھے چکن کڑاہی اور دو روٹی چاہیے۔
choices.en: I'd like chicken karahi and two rotis.
choices.feedback: That's an order!

line.roman: Ji. Aur kuch? Peene ke liye?
line.urdu: جی۔ اور کچھ؟ پینے کے لیے؟
line.en: Sure. Anything else? Something to drink?

choices.roman: Ek paani ki bottle, aur khaane ke baad chai.
choices.urdu: ایک پانی کی بوتل، اور کھانے کے بعد چائے۔
choices.en: A bottle of water, and tea after the meal.
choices.feedback: "Khaane ke baad" = after the meal. Very natural.
Perfectly fine.

line.urdu: یہ لیجیے۔ کھانا کیسا ہے؟
line.en: Here you go. How's the food?

choices.feedback: Compliments go a long way.

choices.roman: Acha hai. Ek roti aur, please.
choices.urdu: اچھا ہے۔ ایک روٹی اور، پلیز۔
choices.en: It's good. One more roti, please.
choices.feedback: "Ek ... aur" = one more. Useful!

line.urdu: شکریہ جی۔ اور کچھ چاہیے؟
line.en: Thank you. Need anything else?

choices.en: No, that's it. The bill, please.
choices.feedback: Short and clear.

choices.roman: Mujhe pyaas lagi hai. Paani aur dein.
choices.urdu: مجھے پیاس لگی ہے۔ پانی اور دیں۔
choices.feedback: Correct — you can ask for the bill afterwards.

line.roman: Ji, bill aath sau rupay hai.
line.urdu: جی، بل آٹھ سو روپے ہے۔
line.en: The bill is eight hundred rupees.

choices.en: Here you are. Thanks a lot!
choices.feedback: "Yeh lijiye" = here you are (polite).
Good practical question.

line.roman: Ji haan, card bhi chalta hai.
line.urdu: جی ہاں، کارڈ بھی چلتا ہے۔
line.en: Yes, card works too.

choices.feedback: All paid!

line.urdu: شکریہ! پھر آئیے گا۔
line.en: Thank you! Do come again.

nodes.end: You ordered a meal, complimented the food and paid — a complete restaurant visit in Urdu.

title: Bargaining in the bazaar
context: You're at a clothes stall in a busy bazaar, looking for a kurta. Prices here are negotiable.
goal: Ask the price, bargain politely, and agree on a deal.

line.urdu: آئیے، آئیے! کیا چاہیے؟
line.en: Come in, come in! What do you need?

choices.feedback: Clear and direct.
It's a clothes shop! Use "Mujhe ek kurta chahiye".

line.roman: Yeh dekhiye, bohat acha kurta hai.
line.urdu: یہ دیکھیے، بہت اچھا کرتا ہے۔
line.en: Look at this one, it's a very nice kurta.

choices.feedback: Good question to ask first.
The most common way to ask a price.

line.urdu: صرف تین ہزار روپے۔
line.en: Only three thousand rupees.

choices.roman: Yeh bohat mehenga hai. Thora kam karein.
choices.urdu: یہ بہت مہنگا ہے۔ تھوڑا کم کریں۔
choices.en: That's very expensive. Please lower it a bit.
choices.feedback: Classic polite bargaining.

choices.roman: Mujhe yeh pasand nahi. Aur kuch hai?
choices.urdu: مجھے یہ پسند نہیں۔ اور کچھ ہے؟
choices.en: I don't like this one. Is there anything else?
choices.feedback: Fine — let's see another one.
You can pay the first price, but in a bazaar a little bargaining is normal.

line.roman: Acha, yeh doosra dekhiye. Yeh do hazaar ka hai.
line.urdu: اچھا، یہ دوسرا دیکھیے۔ یہ دو ہزار کا ہے۔
line.en: Alright, look at this other one. It's two thousand.

choices.roman: Yeh acha hai! Thora kam karein?
choices.urdu: یہ اچھا ہے! تھوڑا کم کریں؟
choices.en: This is nice! Could you lower it a little?
choices.feedback: Nice bargaining.

line.roman: Acha, aap ke liye... dhai hazaar.
line.urdu: اچھا، آپ کے لیے... ڈھائی ہزار۔
line.en: Okay, for you... two and a half thousand.

choices.feedback: A sensible counter-offer.

choices.en: Okay, two and a half thousand.
choices.feedback: A fair deal — you already saved 500.

line.urdu: چلو، ٹھیک ہے۔ دو ہزار۔
line.en: Alright, fine. Two thousand.

choices.en: Thanks a lot! Here you are.
choices.feedback: Deal done!

line.urdu: شکریہ! اور کچھ؟
line.en: Thank you! Anything else?

choices.feedback: Polite finish.

line.urdu: پھر آئیے گا! خدا حافظ۔
line.en: Come again! Goodbye.

nodes.end: You asked a price, bargained politely and bought a kurta.

title: Asking for directions
context: You're lost on your way to the bazaar. You stop a passer-by.
goal: Ask the way, follow the directions, and check the distance.

line.urdu: جی، فرمائیے؟
line.en: Yes, how can I help?

newWords.en: please say (very polite: how can I help?)

choices.en: Excuse me, where is the bazaar?
choices.feedback: Polite and clear.
Understandable, but a bit abrupt. Adding "Maaf kijiye" and "kahan hai" sounds friendlier.
You're the one asking! Try "... kahan hai?".

line.urdu: سیدھا جائیں، پھر دائیں مڑیں۔
line.en: Go straight, then turn right.

choices.roman: Acha, seedha aur phir daayen. Kya yeh door hai?
choices.urdu: اچھا، سیدھا اور پھر دائیں۔ کیا یہ دور ہے؟
choices.en: Okay, straight and then right. Is it far?
choices.feedback: Repeating directions back is a great way to check you understood.

choices.roman: Mujhe samajh nahi aaya. Dobara boliye.
choices.urdu: مجھے سمجھ نہیں آیا۔ دوبارہ بولیے۔
choices.en: I didn't understand. Please say it again.
choices.feedback: Good — no shame in asking again.
He said "daayen" (right), not "baayen" (left). Listen again.

line.roman: Seedha... jaayen. Phir... daayen. Right side.
line.urdu: سیدھا... جائیں۔ پھر... دائیں۔ رائٹ سائیڈ۔
line.en: Go... straight. Then... right. Right side.

choices.roman: Acha, seedha aur phir daayen. Kya yeh door hai?
choices.urdu: اچھا، سیدھا اور پھر دائیں۔ کیا یہ دور ہے؟
choices.en: Okay, straight and then right. Is it far?
choices.feedback: Got it!

line.urdu: نہیں، قریب ہے۔ پانچ منٹ۔
line.en: No, it's close. Five minutes.

choices.feedback: Perfect.
Nice — you checked the detail and thanked him.

line.urdu: کوئی بات نہیں۔ خدا حافظ!
line.en: No problem. Goodbye!

nodes.end: You asked for directions, confirmed them and found out the distance.

title: Visiting someone's home
context: You've been invited to a friend's home for the first time. Their mother (Aunty) opens the door.
goal: Greet the host, make small talk, handle hospitality, and leave politely.

line.urdu: آئیے، آئیے، اندر آئیے۔
line.en: Come in, come in, please come inside.

choices.feedback: "Aunty" is the usual respectful way to address a friend's mother in Pakistan.

choices.roman: Kya main andar aa sakta hoon?
choices.urdu: کیا میں اندر آ سکتا ہوں؟
choices.feedback: Polite, though she's already invited you in! Returning her greeting comes first.

line.roman: Baithiye. Ghar dhoondhne mein mushkil to nahi hui?
line.urdu: بیٹھیے۔ گھر ڈھونڈنے میں مشکل تو نہیں ہوئی؟
line.en: Please sit. You didn't have trouble finding the house?

choices.roman: Nahi, bilkul nahi. Raasta aasaan tha.
choices.urdu: نہیں، بالکل نہیں۔ راستہ آسان تھا۔
choices.en: No, not at all. The way was easy.
choices.feedback: Smooth answer.

choices.roman: Thori si. Pehle main ghalat gali mein chala gaya!
choices.urdu: تھوڑی سی۔ پہلے میں غلط گلی میں چلا گیا!
choices.en: A little. At first I went into the wrong street!
choices.feedback: A friendly, honest answer. A woman would say "chali gayi".
She asked if you had trouble finding the house.

line.urdu: چائے لیں گے یا کچھ ٹھنڈا؟
line.en: Will you have tea or something cold?

choices.feedback: Accepting is gracious.
Polite, but expect the host to insist!

line.roman: Arre, aise kaise? Kuch to lena parega!
line.urdu: ارے، ایسے کیسے؟ کچھ تو لینا پڑے گا!
line.en: Oh, how can that be? You'll have to have something!

nodes.note: Hosts insisting is part of Pakistani hospitality — accepting something small is gracious.

choices.feedback: Good call.

line.roman: Yeh lijiye. Aur samosay bhi lijiye.
line.urdu: یہ لیجیے۔ اور سموسے بھی لیجیے۔
line.en: Here you go. And have some samosas too.

choices.feedback: "Mazay ke" — plural, to match samosay.
Fine. For several samosas you could say "bohat ache hain".

line.roman: Aur lijiye na! Aap ne to kuch khaya hi nahi.
line.urdu: اور لیجیے نا! آپ نے تو کچھ کھایا ہی نہیں۔
line.en: Have more! You've hardly eaten anything.

choices.roman: Bas, shukriya, Aunty. Pet bhar gaya!
choices.urdu: بس، شکریہ آنٹی۔ پیٹ بھر گیا!
choices.en: That's enough, thanks Aunty. I'm full!
choices.feedback: The polite way to stop — warm and clear.
Grammatically right, but it can sound blunt to a host. "Bas, shukriya" is softer.

line.roman: Acha, phir aate rehna. Ghar walon ko salaam kehna.
line.urdu: اچھا، پھر آتے رہنا۔ گھر والوں کو سلام کہنا۔
line.en: Alright, keep visiting. Give my regards to your family.

choices.roman: Ji, zaroor. Bohat shukriya, Aunty. Khuda hafiz!
choices.urdu: جی، ضرور۔ بہت شکریہ آنٹی۔ خدا حافظ!
choices.en: Of course. Thank you so much, Aunty. Goodbye!
choices.feedback: A perfect, polite exit.

line.urdu: خدا حافظ بیٹا!
line.en: Goodbye, dear!

nodes.end: You navigated a home visit: greeting, small talk, hospitality and a polite goodbye.

title: Weekend plans
context: Your friend Hamza calls to make plans for the weekend.
goal: Discuss options, agree on a plan and a time.

line.roman: Yaar, is weekend kya plan hai?
line.urdu: یار، اس ویک اینڈ کیا پلان ہے؟
line.en: Mate, what's the plan this weekend?

choices.roman: Abhi koi plan nahi. Tum batao?
choices.urdu: ابھی کوئی پلان نہیں۔ تم بتاؤ؟
choices.en: No plans yet. What about you?
choices.feedback: "Tum batao" — informal, right for a friend.
Natural! Asking back keeps it going, though.

line.roman: Chalo, Saturday ko cricket khelte hain, phir bahar khaana khayenge.
line.urdu: چلو، سیٹرڈے کو کرکٹ کھیلتے ہیں، پھر باہر کھانا کھائیں گے۔
line.en: Let's play cricket on Saturday, then we'll eat out.

choices.en: Awesome! What time shall we meet?
choices.feedback: "Zabardast" = awesome. Great energy.

choices.roman: Mujhe cricket pasand nahi. Kuch aur karte hain?
choices.urdu: مجھے کرکٹ پسند نہیں۔ کچھ اور کرتے ہیں؟
choices.en: I don't like cricket. Shall we do something else?
choices.feedback: Honest — and you suggested an alternative.

choices.roman: Main nahi jaa sakta. Phir kabhi.
choices.urdu: میں نہیں جا سکتا۔ پھر کبھی۔
choices.en: I can't go. Some other time.
choices.feedback: A polite decline. (Women: "nahi jaa sakti".)

line.urdu: اچھا، تو مووی دیکھتے ہیں؟
line.en: Okay, so shall we watch a movie?

choices.roman: Haan, yeh acha plan hai! Kitne baje?
choices.urdu: ہاں، یہ اچھا پلان ہے! کتنے بجے؟
choices.en: Yes, that's a good plan! What time?
choices.feedback: Agreed!

line.roman: Shaam paanch baje. Main tumhe le loonga.
line.urdu: شام پانچ بجے۔ میں تمہیں لے لوں گا۔
line.en: Five in the evening. I'll pick you up.

choices.feedback: (Women: "intezaar karungi".)

choices.roman: Paanch baje? Thora late, chhe baje?
choices.urdu: پانچ بجے؟ تھوڑا لیٹ، چھ بجے؟
choices.feedback: Good negotiation.

line.urdu: ڈن! سیٹرڈے ملتے ہیں، ضرور۔
line.en: Done! See you Saturday, definitely.

choices.feedback: Natural close.

line.roman: Koi masla nahi, yaar. Agle hafte?
line.urdu: کوئی مسئلہ نہیں یار۔ اگلے ہفتے؟
line.en: No problem, mate. Next week?

choices.feedback: Friendship saved.

line.urdu: چلو، بائے!
line.en: Okay, bye!

nodes.end: You discussed options, made (or postponed) a plan and agreed a time.

title: Catching up with a friend
context: You bump into your friend Ayesha after a long time.
goal: Use casual Urdu, react to news and keep the conversation flowing.

line.roman: Arre! Kitne dinon baad! Kya haal hai?
line.urdu: ارے! کتنے دنوں بعد! کیا حال ہے؟
line.en: Oh! It's been ages! How's it going?

choices.feedback: Relaxed and natural between friends.
Polite and correct ("kaisi" for a woman) — just more formal than you need with a close friend.

line.roman: Main bhi theek. Bas kaam bohat hai aaj kal.
line.urdu: میں بھی ٹھیک۔ بس کام بہت ہے آج کل۔
line.en: I'm fine too. Just a lot of work these days.

choices.roman: Acha? Kaam kaisa chal raha hai?
choices.urdu: اچھا؟ کام کیسا چل رہا ہے؟
choices.feedback: A good follow-up question.
Being overworked isn't really good news! Ask a follow-up instead.

line.roman: Theek hai, lekin boss ne naak mein dam kar diya hai!
line.urdu: ٹھیک ہے، لیکن باس نے ناک میں دم کر دیا ہے!
line.en: It's okay, but my boss is driving me up the wall!

choices.feedback: Showing interest keeps her talking — great listening practice.
Kind, if a bit serious for a joking complaint.

line.roman: Har roz late tak kaam! Khair, tumhari Urdu to kamaal ki ho gayi hai!
line.urdu: ہر روز لیٹ تک کام! خیر، تمہاری اردو تو کمال کی ہو گئی ہے!
line.en: Working late every day! Anyway, your Urdu has become amazing!

choices.roman: Shukriya! Main roz practice karta hoon.
choices.urdu: شکریہ! میں روز پریکٹس کرتا ہوں۔
choices.feedback: (Women: "karti hoon".)
Modest — very natural.

line.roman: Wah! Chalo, kal coffee peete hain?
line.urdu: واہ! چلو، کل کافی پیتے ہیں؟
line.en: Wow! Hey, shall we get coffee tomorrow?

choices.feedback: Perfect.

line.urdu: ڈن! کل ملتے ہیں۔
line.en: Done! See you tomorrow.

nodes.end: You kept a casual conversation flowing with reactions and follow-up questions.

title: A phone call to an office
context: You call a company to speak to Mr Ahmed about a delivery. The receptionist answers.
goal: Ask for someone, introduce yourself, and arrange a callback or leave a message.

line.urdu: جی، رحمان ٹریڈرز۔
line.en: Yes, Rehman Traders.

choices.roman: Kya main Ahmed sahab se baat kar sakta hoon?
choices.urdu: کیا میں احمد صاحب سے بات کر سکتا ہوں؟
choices.en: May I speak to Mr Ahmed?
choices.feedback: Polite and professional. (Women: "kar sakti hoon".)
She already said the company name — it's you who called!

line.roman: Ji, main receptionist bol rahi hoon. Aap ko kis se baat karni hai?
line.urdu: جی، میں ریسیپشنسٹ بول رہی ہوں۔ آپ کو کس سے بات کرنی ہے؟
line.en: This is the receptionist. Who do you want to speak to?

choices.roman: Kya main Ahmed sahab se baat kar sakta hoon?
choices.urdu: کیا میں احمد صاحب سے بات کر سکتا ہوں؟
choices.en: May I speak to Mr Ahmed?
choices.feedback: That's it.

line.roman: Ji, aap kaun bol rahe hain?
line.urdu: جی، آپ کون بول رہے ہیں؟
line.en: May I ask who's speaking?

choices.feedback: (Women: "bol rahi hoon".)

line.roman: Ahmed sahab abhi meeting mein hain. Aap baad mein call kar lein, ya message chhor dein?
line.urdu: احمد صاحب ابھی میٹنگ میں ہیں۔ آپ بعد میں کال کر لیں، یا میسج چھوڑ دیں؟
line.en: Mr Ahmed is in a meeting right now. Would you call later, or leave a message?

choices.roman: Main baad mein call karta hoon. Meeting kitne baje khatam hogi?
choices.urdu: میں بعد میں کال کرتا ہوں۔ میٹنگ کتنے بجے ختم ہوگی؟
choices.en: I'll call later. What time will the meeting end?
choices.feedback: A useful follow-up question.

choices.roman: Message chhor deta hoon: please mujhe call karein.
choices.urdu: میسج چھوڑ دیتا ہوں: پلیز مجھے کال کریں۔
choices.en: I'll leave a message: please call me.
choices.feedback: Clear. (Women: "chhor deti hoon".)

choices.roman: Awaaz nahi aa rahi. Dobara boliye?
choices.urdu: آواز نہیں آ رہی۔ دوبارہ بولیے؟
choices.en: I can't hear you. Could you say it again?
choices.feedback: Fair — phone lines are hard. She'll repeat it.

line.urdu: تقریباً تین بجے۔
line.en: Around three o'clock.

choices.roman: Theek hai, shukriya. Main teen baje call karunga.
choices.urdu: ٹھیک ہے، شکریہ۔ میں تین بجے کال کروں گا۔
choices.en: Okay, thanks. I'll call at three.
choices.feedback: (Women: "karungi".)

line.urdu: جی، آپ کا نمبر؟
line.en: And your number?

choices.roman: Unke paas mera number hai. Shukriya!
choices.urdu: ان کے پاس میرا نمبر ہے۔ شکریہ!
choices.feedback: "Unke paas" = he has (respectful).

line.urdu: جی، ضرور۔ خدا حافظ۔
line.en: Certainly. Goodbye.

nodes.end: You handled a phone call: asked for someone, introduced yourself and arranged next steps.

title: Fixing a misunderstanding
context: Your taxi driver has taken you to Liberty Market, but you wanted Liberty Hotel.
goal: Explain the problem, clarify, negotiate, and stay polite.

line.urdu: لیجیے، آ گئے۔ لبرٹی مارکیٹ۔
line.en: Here we are. Liberty Market.

choices.roman: Maaf kijiye, mujhe Liberty Hotel jaana hai, market nahi.
choices.urdu: معاف کیجیے، مجھے لبرٹی ہوٹل جانا ہے، مارکیٹ نہیں۔
choices.en: Excuse me, I need to go to Liberty Hotel, not the market.
choices.feedback: Clear and polite.
You'd be getting out at the wrong place! Explain where you need to go.
That's for broken things. Say where you need to go: "Mujhe ... jaana hai".

line.roman: Acha? Aap ne to market kaha tha!
line.urdu: اچھا؟ آپ نے تو مارکیٹ کہا تھا!
line.en: Really? You said market!

choices.roman: Galti ho gayi, maazrat. Kya aap hotel le ja sakte hain?
choices.urdu: غلطی ہو گئی، معذرت۔ کیا آپ ہوٹل لے جا سکتے ہیں؟
choices.en: My mistake, sorry. Can you take me to the hotel?
choices.feedback: Taking the blame lightly smooths things over. "Le jaana" = to take (someone).
Clear enough. A softer tone usually gets better results.

line.roman: Theek hai, lekin kiraya thora zyada hoga. Teen sau aur.
line.urdu: ٹھیک ہے، لیکن کرایہ تھوڑا زیادہ ہوگا۔ تین سو اور۔
line.en: Alright, but the fare will be a bit more. Three hundred more.

choices.roman: Aap ka matlab hai teen sau rupay aur?
choices.urdu: آپ کا مطلب ہے تین سو روپے اور؟
choices.en: You mean three hundred rupees more?
choices.feedback: Checking the number is smart.

choices.roman: Yeh bohat zyada hai! Do sau theek hai?
choices.urdu: یہ بہت زیادہ ہے! دو سو ٹھیک ہے؟
choices.en: That's too much! Is two hundred okay?
choices.feedback: Fair negotiation.

line.roman: Ji, teen sau aur. Hotel door hai.
line.urdu: جی، تین سو اور۔ ہوٹل دور ہے۔
line.en: Yes, three hundred more. The hotel is far.

choices.feedback: "Chaliye" = let's go (polite).

line.urdu: چلو، ڈھائی سو۔ بس۔
line.en: Okay, two-fifty. Final.

choices.feedback: Deal.

line.urdu: لیجیے، لبرٹی ہوٹل۔
line.en: Here you are, Liberty Hotel.

choices.en: Thanks a lot, brother. Here you go.
choices.feedback: "Bhai" is a friendly, respectful way to address a man.

line.urdu: شکریہ! خدا حافظ۔
line.en: Thank you! Goodbye.

nodes.end: You explained a mix-up, clarified the fare and stayed polite — real-world recovery skills.

title: Telling a travel story
context: Your cousin Zara heard you went to Murree and wants the full story.
goal: Tell a story in order using linking words and keep your listener engaged.

line.roman: Suna hai tum Murree gaye thay? Kaisa raha?
line.urdu: سنا ہے تم مری گئے تھے؟ کیسا رہا؟
line.en: I heard you went to Murree? How was it?

choices.roman: Bohat mazaa aaya! Pata hai kya hua?
choices.urdu: بہت مزہ آیا! پتا ہے کیا ہوا؟
choices.en: It was so much fun! You know what happened?
choices.feedback: A great hook to start a story.
True, but short answers end conversations. Give her a story!

line.urdu: بس؟ کچھ تو بتاؤ!
line.en: That's it? Tell me something!

choices.roman: Acha, suno. Pata hai kya hua?
choices.urdu: اچھا، سنو۔ پتا ہے کیا ہوا؟
choices.en: Okay, listen. You know what happened?
choices.feedback: Here we go.

line.urdu: نہیں، کیا ہوا؟
line.en: No, what happened?

choices.roman: Pehle hum subah jaldi nikle, lekin raaste mein gaari kharab ho gayi!
choices.urdu: پہلے ہم صبح جلدی نکلے، لیکن راستے میں گاڑی خراب ہو گئی!
choices.en: First we set off early, but on the way the car broke down!
choices.feedback: "Pehle ... lekin ..." — a clear start with a twist.

line.urdu: اوہ نو! پھر؟
line.en: Oh no! Then what?

choices.roman: Phir achanak barish shuru ho gayi, aur hum do ghante intezaar karte rahe.
choices.urdu: پھر اچانک بارش شروع ہو گئی، اور ہم دو گھنٹے انتظار کرتے رہے۔
choices.en: Then suddenly it started raining, and we kept waiting for two hours.
choices.feedback: "Phir achanak" — great storytelling rhythm.

choices.roman: Uske baad hum ghar wapas aa gaye.
choices.urdu: اس کے بعد ہم گھر واپس آ گئے۔
choices.en: After that we came back home.
choices.feedback: Grammatically great, but it ends the story early! Add more detail.

line.urdu: اُف! اتنی مشکل!
line.en: Ugh! So much trouble!

choices.roman: Haan, lekin mazay ki baat yeh hai ke ek chai wale ne hamein muft chai pilayi!
choices.urdu: ہاں، لیکن مزے کی بات یہ ہے کہ ایک چائے والے نے ہمیں مفت چائے پلائی!
choices.en: Yes, but the funny thing is a tea seller gave us free tea!
choices.feedback: "Mazay ki baat yeh hai ke" — perfect for a twist.

line.roman: Haha, wah! Aakhir mein pohanch gaye?
line.urdu: ہاہا، واہ! آخر میں پہنچ گئے؟
line.en: Haha, nice! Did you get there in the end?

choices.roman: Haan, aakhir mein raat ko pohanch gaye. Der aayad durust aayad!
choices.urdu: ہاں، آخر میں رات کو پہنچ گئے۔ دیر آید درست آید!
choices.en: Yes, we finally got there at night. Better late than never!
choices.feedback: An idiom to finish — impressive!

choices.en: Yes, we got there in the end.
choices.feedback: A clear ending.

line.urdu: ہاہا! کمال کی کہانی ہے۔
line.en: Haha! What a story.

nodes.end: You told a full story with linking words — pehle, lekin, phir, achanak, aakhir mein.
